Dumb
dŭm
adj. (unable or unwilling to speak; rendering Hebrew illem, damam, Greek kophos, alalos)
From Anglo-Saxon dumb, mute. The Authorized Version never uses it to mean stupid; it means speechless, whether by affliction, by choice, or by judgment.

Biblical Definition

Dumb means without speech, and Scripture uses it in four ways. It is an affliction God claims sovereignty over: “Who hath made man's mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf…? have not I the LORD?” (Exo 4:11) — spoken to Moses, who was pleading a speech impediment as a disqualification. It is a chosen silence under God's hand: “I was dumb, I opened not my mouth; because thou didst it” (Psa 39:9). It is a judgment on unfaithful ministers — Isaiah's watchmen are “dumb dogs, they cannot bark” (Isa 56:10), the most damning phrase in Scripture for a preacher who will not warn. And supremely, it is the willing silence of the Substitute: “as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth” (Isa 53:7). Against all of it stands the command that the church has no excuse to ignore: “Open thy mouth for the dumb” (Pro 31:8).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines dumb as mute, silent, not speaking — and as destitute of the power of speech, as a dumb beast, noting that it does not signify want of understanding.

expand to see more

DUMB, a. Mute; silent; not speaking.

I was dumb with silence, I held my peace. Ps. xxxix.

2. Destitute of the power of speech; unable to utter articulate sounds; as the dumb brute.

3. Not accompanied with speech; as a dumb show.

Key Scripture

Exo 4:11 — "And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the LORD?"

Isa 53:7 — "He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth."

Pro 31:8 — "Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction."

Isa 56:10 — "His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber."

Modern Corruption

The pulpit made dumb by prudence — silence on whatever costs a hearing, rebranded as winsomeness — while Proverbs 31:8 commands the opposite use of the mouth.

expand to see more

Isaiah 56:10 is a permanent indictment of ministerial silence, and the image is exact: a watchdog that will not bark is worse than useless, because his presence persuades the household it is guarded. A ministry that avoids every subject on which its people are actually being deceived has become a dumb dog, whatever its attendance. And the modern euphemisms for it — being winsome, keeping the main thing the main thing, not being political — are precisely the vocabulary Isaiah's watchmen would have used.

The counterpoise is that Scripture also commends silence, and the church must know which is which. Psalm 39:9 is a saint choosing not to speak because thou didst it — silence under providence, not before error. And Isaiah 53:7 shows the Lamb dumb before His accusers, which is the pattern for suffering wrongfully rather than for teaching. The rule that sorts them is Proverbs 31:8: open thy mouth for the dumb. Speech is owed to those who cannot speak for themselves; silence is permitted about oneself.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew illem (H483), mute, speechless; damam (H1826), to be still, silent; Greek kophos (G2974), blunted in speech or hearing; alalos (G216), without speech.

expand to see more

Hebrew illem (H483) — dumb, unable to speak; the dumb whose cause Pro 31:8 commands the king to plead, and the dumb sheep of Isa 53:7.

Hebrew damam (H1826) — to be silent, still; the psalmist's chosen dumbness under God's hand (Psa 39:9).

Greek kophos (G2974) — blunt, dull; used of both deafness and dumbness, since the two afflictions travel together (Mar 7:37).

Usage

"“Who maketh the dumb, or deaf…? have not I the LORD?” — sovereignty claimed over affliction."

"“They are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark” — the indictment of a silent ministry."

"“Open thy mouth for the dumb” — speech owed to those who have none."
